heading: Pump boundaries — the `PumpBoundary` atom
text:
## Pump boundaries — the `PumpBoundary` atom [RFCS.22]

[RFCS.22] A `PumpBoundary` atom marks one pump of the engine to quiescence
([RARC.5.6.6]). The engine **must** emit one per pump, **including a pump that
fired nothing** — that pump is exactly the one no other atom records, and it is
the case the atom exists for.

**Container-legality `stream`, stream-class `inject`** (field 4).
A replayer **performs** a pump on meeting one, so it is an input the engine was
given rather than an observable it produced, and it **must not** be compared
([RFCS.17.5]).

**The body carries no fire count** (`proto/pump_boundary.proto`). An inject
atom's body is delivered to the engine and never compared, so a count of what
the pump fired — engine output — would be a number a replayer must ignore while
looking like one it should check. What a pump fired is already on the trace, as
the atoms emitted between this boundary and the previous one.

**Why a boundary.** Without one, a trace cannot distinguish
`assert, assert, pump` from `assert, pump, assert, pump`, because a pump that
fires nothing leaves no other trace. The engine records what it did, so a
replayer reproduces it ([LFST.9.2.1]).

**The cadence is read off the trace and declared nowhere.** No header field
carries it; `StreamHeader` reserves field 15 and its name
(`proto/stream_header.proto`, [STYL.2.8.7]).
